title: The 10 Most Valuable Players Left Off USMNT Roster for November Break
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayNov 8, 2026Some big names are missing from Mauricio Pochettino’s squad. / Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty ImagesThe United States men’s national team faces surprise 2026 World Cup qualifiers Haiti twice this November, but some of the country’s leading stars have been omitted from Mauricio Pochettino’s latest roster.

The Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal provides the stage for the upcoming test of the USMNT’s resolve, and it’s seeking to extend a four-match winning streak which began with friendly victories over Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada during September and October.

Pochettino named a youthful squad for those ultimately meaningless matches, and despite restoring many of his most established names for the double bill with Haiti, there remain some high-profile absentees.
With that in mind—and with the help of Transfermarkt—here are the most valuable players who won’t feature for the USMNT this month.

Ricardo Pepi has been left out. / ANP/Getty ImagesChristian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie are the biggest names to have returned to the roster after rests during the previous international break, but they aren’t joined in the 25-man setup by Ricardo Pepi.

The PSV Eindhoven striker only recently returned from injury, making cameos in each of the Dutch club’s last three matches after a month out of action. Pochettino confirmed his absence comes down to a need for more recovery time.

Pochettino will have to compete without the $33.4 million-rated forward, and he’s decided to leave behind another $24.5 million worth of talent in Brenden Aaronson. Worryingly for the Leeds United midfielder, his omission isn‘t down to injury, merely an underwhelming stretch of form which has seen him start just three Premier League games this season.

Valued at $22.3 million each, Johnny Cardoso and Timothy Weah won’t be involved against Haiti, either. The Atlético Madrid midfielder only returned from a thigh injury against Barcelona on Sunday, which explains his omission, but Weah has simply been left out despite registering several goal involvements over the past few weeks with Marseille.

Weah won’t have the chance to add to his 53 international caps, and Yunus Musah will end the calendar year on 50 appearances after also being snubbed. The $20.1 million midfielder has started eight matches for AC Milan in Serie A this season, but has evidently failed to impress Pochettino.

Yunus Musah has been dropped having made the previous roster.  / Fabrizio Carabelli/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesTwo strikers valued at $17.8 million are absent, too. Toronto FC’s Josh Sargent has been snubbed, while Coventry City’s Haji Wright has missed the entirety of the current campaign through a muscle injury and is yet to make his comeback.

Zavier Gozo has only managed a bit-part role for Crystal Palace since his summer switch, making just three appearances in total. The youngster, who is worth $13.4 million, has unsurprisingly been omitted, but Aidan Morris, who shares the exact same valuation, is a more shocking exclusion after an impressive start to life at Middlesbrough.
There’s no place for Tanner Tessmann, who hasn’t made an appearance for the USMNT since April. He’s started the last four matches for Lyon, but that’s not been enough to merit a call-up.
